Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

## Engineering Update — August

**Migration.** The billing service finished its move off the legacy Postgres cluster on August 22, three days after the read replicas were cut over. Write traffic has run on the new cluster for two weeks with no rollback events. The p99 on invoice reads dropped from 340ms to 190ms. We still have two batch jobs pointing at the old host; Priya is retiring those this week, and then we can decommission the cluster.

**Hires.** Two engineers joined this month. Sam Okonkwo started August 4 on the platform side and has already landed the queue retry fix. Dana Reyes started August 18 on billing and is pairing with Priya through the batch job cleanup. That puts us at twelve. Both are through onboarding; if you have context on the old cluster, they want it.

**The slip.** Reporting exports will not ship September 1. We hit an undocumented rate limit on the export API that caps us at 200 requests per minute, which makes the current design unworkable for accounts over 50,000 rows. Marcus is redesigning around a chunked job. New date is September 26. Sales has been told, and the two customers who asked for this know.

Questions in the channel or find me.

The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

## Engineering Update — August (revised)

**The slip, again.** Reporting exports will not ship September 26 either. The new date is October 17.

The chunked job design works against the 200 requests per minute rate limit, and Marcus had it passing on staging by September 8. Then we ran it against a real account: exports for customers with more than 200,000 rows take 41 minutes, and the export API expires its job tokens at 30. Refreshing the token mid-run restarts the export from row zero. That is a limit of the vendor API, not our code.

We have two options. Ask the vendor to raise the token TTL, which their support desk has not committed to. Or persist partial results and stitch them, which is roughly three weeks of work for Marcus and Dana. We are doing both: the ticket is filed, and the stitching work starts Monday because we cannot wait on an answer that may not come.

October 17 assumes the stitching approach and no further surprises from the vendor API. I set the earlier date on a staging result without testing a large account first. That was my call and it cost us three weeks.

Sales knows. I am telling the two customers myself today.
